description: Device searches at the border operate under a reduced-protection doctrine in several countries, so a traveller can be required to unlock a phone with no suspicion standard that would be required inland.

aspect: What is on an Iranian's phone
description: Contacts in Iran, Persian-language messaging groups, VPN apps and family photos all read as flags to an officer working from a threat template.
Hours in secondary routinely cost the onward flight.

aspect: Refusing is not an option in practice
description: Declining to unlock can mean device seizure for weeks, or denial of entry for a non-citizen. Consent is nominal.

aspect: SCENARIO - the phone he had to unlock
description: Returning from Istanbul, Omid is sent to secondary. An officer asks him to unlock his phone. It contains a Telegram group of eighteen relatives, photographs of a protest he walked past in 2022, and a VPN app he uses to read the news. He unlocks it, because the alternative is a seized device and a missed connection.
money_note: Missed connection and one hotel night.
energy_note: Consent, offered at the only price available.
